summary:
Albireo Brillante is a space strategy, resource management, and survival video game developed in GDevelop by Matías Salinas and Juan Sebastián Cabral. The project challenges players to establish and manage self-sustaining human colonies on the Moon and Mars through a grid-based building system, real-time periodic production, and interactive minigames for crop watering, oxygen pumping, anti-radiation shielding, and structural repair.
To address the challenge of simulating life in hostile environments, the game integrates logical progression rules, material management, and constant threats such as solar radiation, oxygen depletion, and base wear. This project is important because it encourages strategic thinking and decision-making under pressure, bringing the real-world challenges of space exploration and colonization closer to players in an educational and interactive way.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Albireo Brillante is a 2D top-down space colony strategy and management video game. Players depart from Earth, select a habitable destination on a star map (Mars or the Moon), and build a self-sustaining base using an interactive grid. To survive, they must balance real-time resources (Materials, Oxygen, Radiation, and Base Integrity) and complete interactive maintenance mini-games, such as watering greenhouses, repairing structural damage, and activating anti-radiation shields.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Interactive learning: Introduces real space exploration concepts, such as the difference between habitable worlds and gas giants, life-support management, and cosmic radiation hazards.
  • Strategic thinking: Encourages decision-making under pressure, finite resource planning, and quick problem-solving through mini-games.
  • Accessibility: With an intuitive visual interface and simple mouse controls, anyone can play without prior experience in complex strategy games.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

To spark scientific and space curiosity in players through digital entertainment, demonstrating how technology and environmental management are essential for human survival beyond Earth. It also serves as a practical example of how engaging educational games with deep mechanics can be built using accessible game engines.

4. Tools, programming languages, hardware, and software used

  • Game Engine: GDevelop 5 (visual event-based programming using conditions, actions, scene variables, timers, and layer management).
  • Graphic Design & Editing: Piskel (built into GDevelop for sprites and UI elements), transparent .png image editing tools, and 2D pixel art and illustrated assets.
  • Hardware: Standard PC/Laptop with a mouse for real-time gameplay and UI testing.

5. In what sense is your project creative?

  • Genre fusion: Combines classic city-building mechanics with active pop-up maintenance mini-games, keeping the player engaged rather than acting as a passive observer.
  • Scientific and narrative coherence: The star map deliberately excludes uninhabitable gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn, adapting survival rules to the real conditions of Mars or the Moon.
  • Custom visual identity: Integrates custom-illustrated control consoles (such as the repair drone and shield panel) over a clean 2D environment.

6. What factors did your team take into account?

  • Technical feasibility and scope: Transitioned from an initial 3D prototype to a 2D top-down environment to achieve precise grid placement, smoother performance, and clearer visuals within the project timeline.
  • User Experience (UX): Implemented separate layers (UI and Minijuego), tile-occupation blockers, and visual alerts to prevent accidental clicks while building.
  • Difficulty balance: Calibrated building costs, 5-second production cycles, and progressive radiation wear to maintain a fair and engaging challenge.
